a: Build projects, read docs, practice problems, and review your own code weekly.
Show 2–4 solid projects with README, live demo, and clear problem/solution.
Quantify impact, list relevant stack, link GitHub, keep to one page when possible.
Practice arrays/strings/trees/graphs, speak your thoughts, test edge cases.
Practice requirements, estimates, APIs, data model, scaling, and trade-offs.
Start with docs/bugs, read CONTRIBUTING.md, make small PRs, communicate clearly.
Feeling behind is common; track progress, ask questions, ship small wins.
A mentor gives feedback and career context; come with specific questions.
Schedule weekly learning time; depth in one stack beats shallow buzzwords.
Over-communicate, document decisions, protect focus blocks, keep reliable internet.
Be kind and specific; prefer questions; praise good patterns; own your merges.
Sleep, breaks, realistic scope, and saying no protect long-term productivity.
